title: INDIAN NAVY SET TO COMMISSION SECOND INDIGENOUS DIVING SUPPORT VESSEL 'NIPUN'
body_text:
The Indian Navy is set to commission Nipun , the second Diving Support Vessel (DSV) of the Nistar-class, on 31 Aug 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The induction of the specialised vessel will mark an important addition to the Navy’s deep-sea diving and underwater support capabilities and herald the beginning of a new chapter in the ship’s journey from construction to operational service.
Indigenously designed and constructed by Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), Visakhapatnam , Nipun represents a significant milestone in India’s pursuit of self-reliance in defence shipbuilding. The vessel was delivered to the Indian Navy on 30 Jul 2026 , following completion of an extensive programme of outfitting and trials. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2292073
Nipun is a purpose-built platform designed to support a wide spectrum of diving and underwater operations . The ship is equipped with modern diving systems and underwater intervention capabilities , enabling sustained support to divers operating in demanding conditions at sea . It will also augment the Indian Navy’s capability to support submarine rescue operations.
The ship incorporates modern systems for navigation, platform management and precise station keeping, complemented by specialised facilities for diving, underwater intervention and medical support. These capabilities enable Nipun to function as an integrated platform for complex operations beneath the surface.
The forthcoming commissioning of Nipun will further strengthen the Indian Navy’s ability to undertake specialised diving and underwater missions across India’s maritime areas of interest. The induction of this indigenously built platform also reflects the growing capability of the country’s shipbuilding ecosystem to deliver technologically advanced and specialised vessels in support of the Navy’s operational requirements.

enrichment.summary: The Indian Navy will commission INS Nipun, the second Diving Support Vessel (DSV) of the Nistar-class, on 31 August 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. Built indigenously by Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam, and delivered on 30 July 2026, the vessel is equipped with modern diving systems, underwater intervention capabilities, and facilities to support submarine rescue operations.
enrichment.context: Diving Support Vessels are specialised naval platforms that enable deep-sea diving, underwater intervention, and submarine rescue operations, capabilities critical for a navy operating in contested and deep maritime environments. The Nistar-class programme, built entirely by Hindustan Shipyard Limited (a Defence PSU), is part of India's broader push toward self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in naval shipbuilding, reducing dependence on foreign-built specialised vessels for niche operational roles like submarine rescue support. Submarine rescue capability has been a strategic gap for many navies, and indigenous DSVs like Nipun strengthen India's ability to respond to submarine distress situations in its area of maritime interest, complementing existing Deep Submergence Rescue Vessel (DSRV) assets. This induction also reflects the maturing capacity of India's shipbuilding ecosystem, moving beyond conventional warships to technologically complex, specialised support vessels.
